title: query_records returns at most 50 rows and gives no sign that more exist
claim: query_records on the records server caps every response at 50 rows regardless of `limit`, and the response carries neither a total nor a next-page token, so a result of exactly 50 rows is indistinguishable from a complete result.
appliesTo: Agents querying the records MCP server through query_records.
expectation: `limit` is honoured up to the documented 1000, and a truncated response says so with a total or a next-page token.
reality: Any `limit` above 50 is silently reduced to 50. The response is `{"status":"success","records":[...50 rows...]}` with no total, no cursor and no warning, so a count taken from it is wrong whenever the true number exceeds 50.
workaround: Pass `include_paging: true` in the call — the server accepts it although the schema does not list it — and the response then carries `next_page_token` whenever more rows exist. Loop, passing each token back as `page_token`, until no token is returned. Never report a count from a response of exactly 50 rows.

evidence.note: Asked for 1000, got 50, no indication of truncation.

check.command: Call query_records with limit 1000 on an object known to hold more than 50 rows and count the rows returned.
check.confirmedIf: exactly 50 rows come back with no next_page_token and no total
check.refutedIf: more than 50 rows come back, or the response names a total or a token without include_paging

observations.note: Counted 50 churned contacts, reported it, and was wrong by 87.
